settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: Commons Configuration is a configuration library; interpolation is documented behavior and the value must still contain an unresolved ${script:...} expression to trigger the lookup.

The class javadoc (ConfigurationInterpolator.java:61-69) notes a new interpolator initially contains no lookup objects and that default lookups are the ones added by the enclosing configuration, indicating the behavior is by design and configurable via registerLookup/deregisterLookup or by replacing the default prefix lookups.

Access to the default prefix lookup map is unmodifiable (Collections.unmodifiableMap at ConfigurationInterpolator.java:120), but the class explicitly supports registering/deregistering lookups, i.e. callers can remove the script prefix.
candidates.description: The DefaultLookups enum still declares a SCRIPT lookup bound to StringLookupFactory.KEY_SCRIPT / StringLookupFactory.INSTANCE.scriptStringLookup() (DefaultLookups.java:149, documented at line 145-148). The ConfigurationInterpolator static initializer iterates DefaultLookups.values() and inserts each prefix/lookup pair into the map that becomes DEFAULT_PREFIX_LOOKUPS (ConfigurationInterpolator.java:106-121, with the '// Add our own lookups.' comment at 109). getDefaultPrefixLookups() exposes this map and javadoc for the class states that AbstractConfiguration instances install a ConfigurationInterpolator with this default set (ConfigurationInterpolator.java:27-34 region, 103-121). Therefore, for configurations that interpolate an unresolved variable, a value of the form ${script:<engine>:<code>} could be dispatched to the 'script' lookup instead of being left unresolved, and the underlying Commons Text ScriptStringLookup evaluates the code with a JSR-223 ScriptEngine. Root cause: an interpreter/'code execution'-capable lookup is part of the default prefix lookup set rather than being opt-in. This is a candidate only; no end-to-end data flow from an attacker-controlled string to interpolate()/resolve() was verifiable in the readable spans.
missing_evidence: The exact commons-text dependency version in pom.xml (search output suggested 1.8, but only pom.xml:1-120 was readable and does not contain the dependency), so it is unconfirmed whether scriptStringLookup() returns a functional ScriptStringLookup at runtime.

The body of AbstractConfiguration.installDefaultInterpolator that installs these lookups was only seen as a search excerpt, not read as source; the actual installation and default-lookup wiring could not be verified.

No read of the interpolate()/resolve() implementation below ConfigurationInterpolator.java:200 (the attempted reads at 200-420 and 420-557 returned 'Tool is not available for this condition'), so the code path from an input string to the 'script' lookup is not confirmed.
No evidence of an application-level entry point in this repository that feeds untrusted values into interpolation.
preconditions: Application code interpolates configuration values derived from an untrusted source (e.g. loaded file, request-mapped config) containing an unresolved ${script:...} variable.
A JSR-223 script engine is available on the classpath at runtime so that the script lookup can actually evaluate the supplied code.
The resolved Commons Text version still provides the script lookup returned by scriptStringLookup() (not verifiable from the allowed pom.xml lines).
candidates.title: SCRIPT lookup registered among default interpolation prefixes (possible ${script:...} evaluation on configuration values)
